narrative.gap_prioritization_md: The six-factor prioritization formula assigns a Priority Score (1-5 scale) to each of the 17 categories. All 17 categories are ranked. Tier 1 (Act Now) identifies gaps where Zennify has immediate product solutions, peer gap is large, and stakeholder readiness is confirmed. Priority Score = (0.25 × Gap Size) + (0.20 × Peer Comparison) + (0.15 × Strategic Alignment) + (0.15 × Implementation Complexity) + (0.15 × Investment Efficiency) + (0.10 × Stakeholder Readiness).
narrative.recommendations_md:
[ROOT CAUSE — SITUATION] CCB operates a three-layer data architecture — Snowflake (servicing DW, confirmed via Software Engineer JD [E-067]), Azure SQL Database (operational [E-068]), and Salesforce Data Cloud (CDP in active build [E-051]) — without an integration orchestration layer connecting them. The LOS upgrade to ICE Empower is in active transition, led by Neil Merritt (SVP Product Strategy, hired Nov 2023 [E-076]), with architecture decisions being made NOW.
[ROOT CAUSE — COMPLICATION] Without MuleSoft, three consequences compound simultaneously: (1) Salesforce Data Cloud cannot ingest real-time servicing data from Snowflake, limiting personalization for 700K+ customers [E-067, E-051]; (2) Peoples Bank legacy core data cannot be unified into CCB's Salesforce customer record without a dedicated integration layer [E-004, E-074]; (3) the LOS transition from legacy system to ICE Empower requires all downstream integrations (Salesforce, Black Knight MSP, Snowflake) to be redesigned — and MuleSoft architecture must be established BEFORE the LOS go-live or it becomes 10x harder to add post-deployment [E-041].
[QUESTION] How can CCB integrate its three-layer data stack, unify Peoples Bank customer records, and establish the ICE Empower LOS integration architecture — all within the 12-18 month window before LOS go-live?
[SOLUTION — ANSWER] Zennify implements MuleSoft API-led connectivity as CCB's integration backbone: a real-time bridge between ICE Empower → Salesforce → Snowflake → Data Cloud. MuleSoft has pre-built connectors for Salesforce (native), Snowflake (REST), and ICE ecosystem tools. Tom Clark's Cadence Bank experience (2015-2022: integrated two legacy banks onto one platform for 6,500 employees [E-062]) provides the architectural intuition — Zennify provides the Salesforce-specific MuleSoft delivery expertise. Phase 1 (Q2-Q3 2026): LOS integration architecture design. Phase 2 (Q3-Q4 2026): Peoples Bank data unification. Phase 3 (Q1 2027): Real-time Data Cloud feeds activated.
[ROOT CAUSE — SITUATION] CCB has deployed Omilia IVA (voice AI, active in contact center [E-068]), LLMs for natural language contact center workflows (Workflow Analyst JD: 'prototype and implement NL features using LLMs and GenAI' [E-068]), an AI virtual assistant on Cornerstone Servicing portal since April 2023 [E-048], and CEO Scott Almy committed in December 2024 to 'investing in conversational AI, chatbots, ML, and process automation' [E-009]. CCB has 700,000 customer relationships [E-051] and 60+ B2B institutional banking clients [E-023].
[ROOT CAUSE — COMPLICATION] CCB's AI deployment is fragmented across three unconnected platforms: Omilia IVA (voice), active LLMs (chat/NLP), and the Salesforce Service Cloud (existing CRM). These platforms do not share context — an agent handling a Cornerstone Servicing call cannot see the borrower's Salesforce CRM record in real time. Without governance, each AI deployment creates separate compliance risk, separate data handling, and separate audit trails. The Fitch RPS3 servicer rating [E-052] is explicitly based on 'comprehensive enterprise-wide compliance management' — fragmented AI threatens this. Meanwhile, the 93.97% efficiency ratio [E-007] demands contact center deflection at scale, which requires a unified AI platform, not three disconnected tools.
[QUESTION] How can CCB unify its fragmented AI deployments under enterprise governance, extend AI to 700K borrowers and 60+ institutional clients, and demonstrate measurable efficiency improvement to the board?
[SOLUTION — ANSWER] Zennify deploys AgentForce on Service Cloud as the enterprise AI governance layer: it wraps the existing Omilia IVA and LLM workflows within Salesforce's Einstein Trust Layer, providing unified audit trails, data grounding controls, and cross-platform context. Phase 1: AgentForce contact center agents for Cornerstone Servicing (routine inquiries: payment history, escrow, payoff quotes — for 60+ FI clients first). Phase 2: Borrower-facing agents across 700K+ consumer relationships (loan status, document upload, rate inquiries). Phase 3: Proactive outreach agents triggered by Data Cloud behavioral signals. The pitch to Tom Clark: 'You built the foundation. AgentForce is the Salesforce-native platform for everything you already deployed.'
[ROOT CAUSE — SITUATION] CCB is actively building a Salesforce Data Cloud personalization engine for 700,000+ customer relationships (confirmed in Salesforce Developer II JD: 'actively building a personalization engine using Salesforce Data Cloud' [E-022, E-051]). Simultaneously, Marketing Cloud is being partially replaced by Surefire CRM (ICE Mortgage Technology) for LO-specific email marketing, with Heather Woods leading the migration [E-038]. Peoples Bank closed March 2, 2026, adding a second customer universe [E-074].
[ROOT CAUSE — COMPLICATION] Three risks compound the active Data Cloud build: (1) The MC→Surefire migration creates a data split — LO-specific customer contacts in Surefire, enterprise marketing contacts in Marketing Cloud — creating two separate customer marketing records that will drift out of sync without a bridge [E-038]. (2) Peoples Bank adds ~$1.5B in customer relationships that are not yet connected to the Data Cloud personalization engine, fragmenting the '700K customer' universe before it's even unified [E-004, E-074]. (3) The Data Cloud build is being done without external Salesforce partner expertise in banking-specific Data Cloud implementations, which creates technical debt risk in the data model.
[QUESTION] How can CCB accelerate the Data Cloud personalization build, prevent Marketing Cloud fragmentation, and extend the unified profile to include Peoples Bank customers and real-time servicing data?
[SOLUTION — ANSWER] Zennify accelerates the Data Cloud implementation with Salesforce-certified Data Cloud architects: (1) Build the Surefire→Data Cloud bridge that keeps LO customer data unified with the MC enterprise data, protecting the Marketing Cloud license; (2) Add Peoples Bank core banking data as a new Data Cloud source stream; (3) Connect Snowflake servicing data to Data Cloud via MuleSoft (cross-recommendation dependency with ). Zennify has Salesforce-specific Data Cloud methodology for mortgage banking — including MISMO data standard compliance — that CCB's internal team is building from scratch.
[ROOT CAUSE — SITUATION] nCino is confirmed deployed at CCB — validated by Vanessa Bustos Sanchez, VP Treasury Client Onboarding [E-057]. nCino runs entirely on the Salesforce Platform, meaning CCB is already paying for the Salesforce infrastructure that supports nCino. nCino's product suite includes Mortgage Analytics, Operations Analytics, and Incentive Compensation modules not confirmed as active at CCB.
[ROOT CAUSE — COMPLICATION] CCB's commercial banking analytics currently depend on a mix of nCino's core data and external BI tools (Power BI, Tableau [E-068]), creating reporting that is slower and less integrated than what nCino Analytics provides natively. Loan officer incentive compensation is managed outside nCino (no Incentive Compensation module confirmed), creating manual reconciliation risk across 150+ offices and 15+ JV companies [E-075]. Operations Analytics would provide the pipeline-level visibility that underpins the efficiency ratio improvement story for CFO Paul Woo [E-007].
[QUESTION] How can CCB maximize the value of its existing nCino and Salesforce investment by activating analytics modules that are available on the current contract?
[SOLUTION — ANSWER] Zennify configures nCino Mortgage Analytics (origination pipeline KPIs), Operations Analytics (processing efficiency, SLA compliance), and Incentive Compensation (LO pay calculation, JV company performance) — all on the existing Salesforce infrastructure. This is a zero-procurement-cycle opportunity: no new vendor, no new contract, no new security review. Zennify's nCino practice brings pre-built analytics templates for mortgage banking that accelerate time-to-insight from months to weeks. Vanessa Bustos Sanchez is the confirmed internal champion with hands-on nCino experience.
[ROOT CAUSE — SITUATION] CCB's analytics stack includes Tableau (deployed, confirmed via SVP Toby Gallegos [E-058]), Black Knight RAP (ML risk analytics [E-068]), RiskExec (compliance analytics [E-065]), and Power BI (accessible via M365 [E-063]). Data Cloud is in active build [E-051]. However, no Salesforce-embedded analytics (CRM Analytics / Einstein Analytics) is confirmed deployed, meaning loan officers and commercial bankers must leave Salesforce to access analytics insights.
[ROOT CAUSE — COMPLICATION] Analytics outside Salesforce means: (1) LOs toggle between Salesforce (loan pipeline) and Tableau (performance dashboards) — creating app switching friction for CCB's #1-ranked LOs (7.03 units/month [E-074]); (2) Servicing analytics in Tableau cannot be triggered by Salesforce Data Cloud behavioral signals — the personalization engine being built [E-022] will need an analytics layer to surface insights IN the workflow, not in a separate tab; (3) As Data Cloud matures, Einstein Discovery's predictive capabilities (next-best-action, churn risk, cross-sell timing) require CRM Analytics as the activation layer.
[QUESTION] How can CCB surface mortgage and servicing analytics directly within the Salesforce workflow that LOs already live in, leveraging the Data Cloud build as the analytics data source?
[SOLUTION — ANSWER] Zennify implements CRM Analytics (Einstein Analytics) embedded directly in Salesforce Sales and Service Cloud, with Data Cloud as the primary data source: (1) LO Performance Dashboards in Salesforce (loan volume, pipeline velocity, pull-through rate); (2) Servicing Portfolio Analytics for Cornerstone Servicing (60+ FI clients); (3) Einstein Discovery next-best-action for mortgage officers (triggered by Data Cloud behavioral signals). Sequence dependency: Data Cloud build completes first; CRM Analytics activates the Data Cloud intelligence in-platform.
[ROOT CAUSE — SITUATION] CCB operates 15+ JV mortgage companies with 100+ builder relationships [E-075]. In November 2025, Ironcrest Mortgage launched with Stone Martin Builders (Alabama); in July 2025, Table Rock Mortgage launched with Tresidio Homes (Idaho) [E-077]. Lonnie Jenkins (VP Builder Division) confirmed funded $2.2B in builder forward commitments in 2024 [E-075]. Experience Cloud is deployed as part of CCB's 6-cloud Salesforce footprint [E-051] but no JV partner portal use case is confirmed built on it.
[ROOT CAUSE — COMPLICATION] Each new JV mortgage company (15+ active and growing) requires: branded digital borrower experience, LO workflow tools, mortgage product access, performance reporting for the builder partner, and CCB operational oversight. Without a standardized portal template, each new JV launch requires custom development — ad-hoc, slow, and expensive. The JV program is CCB's key national mortgage growth engine; its scalability is constrained by the technology infrastructure that supports each new launch. As the JV count grows from 15 to 20, 25, and beyond, the marginal cost of each new JV launch must decrease, not increase.
[QUESTION] How can CCB standardize the JV mortgage company launch process, give builder partners a branded self-service digital experience, and track cross-JV performance centrally — enabling the JV program to scale without proportional operational overhead?
[SOLUTION — ANSWER] Zennify builds the Experience Cloud JV Partner Portal template on CCB's existing Salesforce Platform: a branded, configurable portal that each new builder partner gets as their digital interface. Build once; configure per JV: each new JV launch (Ironcrest, Table Rock, and future) gets a CCB-powered branded experience in days, not months. Data Cloud ( dependency) provides cross-JV customer analytics. Lonnie Jenkins's builder relationship team gets centralized performance visibility across all 15+ JVs. Each new builder JV becomes a standard Zennify deployment — incremental revenue for both Zennify and CCB.
[ROOT CAUSE — SITUATION] CCB's security infrastructure includes Okta (IAM/SSO/MFA for 3,000 team members [E-062]), Snyk (DevSecOps scanning), Azure Key Vault (secrets management), and a dedicated IT Security Engineer (Nickesh P., 3+ years [E-071]). CCB is also actively recruiting a Director of Integrated Security to replace the departed CISO Ionel Chila [E-078]. 700,000+ customer records and Peoples Bank integration data are stored in Salesforce.
[ROOT CAUSE — COMPLICATION] Three security gaps simultaneously escalate: (1) CISO gap creates a window where security program ownership is unclear — the new Director of Integrated Security will inherit a Salesforce environment without data-layer protection [E-078]; (2) Peoples Bank integration (March 2026, $1.5B) adds agricultural, small business, and personal banking data from a legacy institution into CCB's Salesforce instance — without Shield, there is no field-level encryption or field audit trail on this newly integrated data [E-004, E-074]; (3) The 2023 third-party breach [E-051], while resolved, demonstrated CCB's exposure to service-provider data handling — Shield's Event Monitoring provides real-time visibility into Salesforce data access patterns that external TPRM cannot replicate.
[QUESTION] How can CCB establish enterprise-grade Salesforce data protection, demonstrate FRB exam-readiness, and give the incoming Director of Integrated Security the platform-layer security controls needed to govern 700K+ customer records across CCB and Peoples Bank?
[SOLUTION — ANSWER] Zennify implements Salesforce Shield (Platform Encryption + Event Monitoring + Field Audit Trail) before or concurrent with the CISO hire: (1) Platform Encryption: field-level encryption for sensitive Salesforce records (SSNs, account numbers, PII) — FRB exam-ready from day one; (2) Event Monitoring: real-time visibility into who accesses what Salesforce data, when, and from where — satisfies OCC/FRB data security requirements; (3) Field Audit Trail: 10-year audit trail on all field changes — critical for Peoples Bank integration data governance. The incoming Director of Integrated Security inherits a governed, documented Salesforce security posture rather than an ungoverned environment.
[ROOT CAUSE — SITUATION] CCB operates Salesforce Sales Cloud and Service Cloud for CRM and service management, but not Salesforce Financial Services Cloud (FSC) mortgage-specific templates and data models. CCB's LOS upgrade (ICE Empower) is actively underway, led by Neil Merritt (SVP Product Strategy, from Newrez LLC where he led similar LOS transitions [E-076, E-041]). 150+ mortgage offices across 45 states use Salesforce for loan pipeline management [E-001].
[ROOT CAUSE — COMPLICATION] Sales Cloud and Service Cloud use generic CRM data models — designed for any industry. The mortgage origination workflow (lead-to-application, rate lock, underwriting, closing, post-close servicing onboarding) requires mortgage-specific objects, field sets, and automation that generic Sales Cloud requires expensive custom development to replicate. Without FSC, each of CCB's 150+ offices runs a partially customized Salesforce environment — creating inconsistent LO workflows, reporting gaps, and technical debt. The LOS upgrade creates a natural re-architecture window: when ICE Empower goes live and MuleSoft creates the integration layer, that is the moment to implement the FSC mortgage data model so that all three systems (ICE Empower + Salesforce FSC + MuleSoft) are designed together.
[QUESTION] How can CCB replace the custom-developed mortgage workflow workarounds in Sales/Service Cloud with a purpose-built FSC mortgage data model, timed to the ICE Empower go-live?
[SOLUTION — ANSWER] Zennify implements Salesforce Financial Services Cloud (FSC) Mortgage Banking: pre-built Residential Loan Application objects, LO activity management, referral partner tracking (25+ national builders), and a standardized loan pipeline data model that connects to ICE Empower via MuleSoft. This is a sequencing recommendation: MuleSoft architecture → FSC implementation → AgentForce in FSC context. Neil Merritt's Newrez background means he understands FSC mortgage templates — Zennify brings the Salesforce implementation expertise to execute on his product roadmap.
narrative.roadmap_md: The phased roadmap sequences all 8 Zennify recommendations by implementation dependency, strategic urgency, and stakeholder readiness. Phase 1 targets the three CRITICAL recommendations that address the LOS window, efficiency ratio narrative, and Data Cloud fragmentation risk. Phase 4 represents full level 4 Managed maturity — achievable in 18-24 months with consistent platform investment.
